text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Some 250 Arab bankers and financiers ended a two-day conference in Beirut with recommendations urging Arab countries to undertake further economic reforms.
-President Hrawi says in his independence day speech that the country needs constitutional reforms and administrative reconstruction.
-Rightwing Lebanese Christian leaders have announced the formation of an opposition front to regain "lost sovereignty".

-Washington is mulling whether to cancel the ban on the travel of Americans to Lebanon ahead of the first meeting of a consultative group of nations in the U.S. capital next month to help finance Lebanon's reconstruction.
-French President Chirac expresses his confidence in Lebanon's future in a message of cogratulations to his Lebanese counterpart Hrawi on Lebanon's 53rd independence day.
-Enviromental experts to arrive from Germany on November 26 to study 36 containers in Beirut port suspected to contain toxic plastic waste imported from Germany.
-Foreign Minister Fares Boues says Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu may launch a war in the region to break the deadlock in Arab-Israeli peace talks.
